0xparc.label: 0xPARC
0xparc.plain: A research group that supports applied research on Ethereum and other decentralized platforms, with a focus on programmable cryptography.

accept-encoding.label: Accept-Encoding
accept-encoding.plain: The HTTP request header where a browser lists the compression formats it can decode, such as gzip, br and zstd.

agent2agent.label: Agent2Agent
agent2agent.plain: An open protocol that lets AI agents built by different companies find each other and hand off tasks.

ai-gateway.label: AI Gateway
ai-gateway.plain: Cloudflare's proxy for calls to AI models. It logs requests and responses, counts tokens and cost, and can cache or rate-limit calls.

ai-hallucination.label: hallucination
ai-hallucination.plain: When an AI model confidently states something false or invented, like describing an object that isn't in the picture.

aliasing.label: Aliasing
aliasing.plain: False patterns, like jagged edges or shimmering moire, that appear when detail finer than the sampling grid gets sampled anyway.

amd-sev.label: AMD SEV
amd-sev.plain: Secure Encrypted Virtualization: an AMD processor feature that encrypts each virtual machine's memory with its own key, hiding it from the host.

anchor-positioning.label: CSS anchor positioning
anchor-positioning.plain: A CSS feature that places one element relative to another, such as a tooltip pinned to its button, without JavaScript measuring positions.

apple-t2.label: Apple T2
apple-t2.plain: A security chip in Intel-based Macs from 2017 onward that stores encryption keys and Touch ID data and checks the startup software.

av1.label: AV1
av1.plain: A royalty-free video codec from the Alliance for Open Media. AVIF images are single AV1 frames stored in an image file.

av2.label: AV2
av2.plain: The video codec that follows AV1, from the Alliance for Open Media. Like AV1, it can also compress single still images.

avif.label: AVIF
avif.plain: An image format that stores a picture compressed with the AV1 video codec. Every current major browser can display it.

bao.label: Bao
bao.plain: A format and tool built on BLAKE3 that lets you verify any slice of a file against its root hash while streaming it.

base32.label: Base32
base32.plain: A way to write binary data using 32 characters, letters and digits, so it can be printed, typed or put in a URL safely.

base64.label: Base64
base64.plain: A way to write binary data as plain text using 64 safe characters. It makes the data about a third larger.

baseline.label: Baseline
baseline.plain: A label for web features that work in the current versions of all the major browsers: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari.

bd-rate.label: BD-rate
bd-rate.plain: Bjøntegaard delta rate: the average share of bytes one encoder saves over another at equal quality, read off their size and quality curves.

bfcache.label: bfcache
bfcache.plain: The back/forward cache: the browser keeps a page frozen in memory when you leave, so Back or Forward restores it instantly with its state intact.

bgv.label: BGV
bgv.plain: A fully homomorphic encryption scheme by Brakerski, Gentry and Vaikuntanathan that computes exactly on encrypted integers and runs fixed-depth circuits without bootstrapping.

binding.label: binding
binding.plain: A named handle in a Worker's environment that connects its code to a resource, such as a database, a storage bucket or another Worker.

bittorrent.label: BitTorrent
bittorrent.plain: A file sharing protocol that splits a file into pieces so many computers each upload and download parts of it at once.

blake3.label: BLAKE3
blake3.plain: A fast cryptographic hash function. It hashes a file as a tree of chunks, so work runs in parallel and parts can be verified alone.

blink.label: Blink
blink.plain: The browser engine behind Chrome, Edge and other Chromium-based browsers.

blockchain.label: blockchain
blockchain.plain: A shared ledger copied across many computers, with records grouped into blocks chained together by hashes so past entries can't be quietly changed.

boolean-circuit.label: Boolean circuit
boolean-circuit.plain: A computation written as a network of logic gates (AND, OR, NOT) that turns input bits into output bits.

bootloader.label: bootloader
bootloader.plain: The small program that runs first when a device powers on, checking and loading the next stage of software until the operating system starts.

brotli.label: Brotli
brotli.plain: A compression algorithm from Google built for the web. It ships with a built-in dictionary of common web text, which helps on small files.

browser-compat-data.label: browser-compat-data
browser-compat-data.plain: MDN's open dataset recording which version of each browser supports each web feature.

browser-run.label: Browser Run
browser-run.plain: Cloudflare's service for controlling a headless browser from a Worker, to render pages, take screenshots or make PDFs.

bt-601.label: BT.601
bt-601.plain: A video standard whose matrix converts red, green and blue into one brightness and two colour channels, with red weighted at 0.299 of brightness.

bun.label: Bun
bun.plain: A JavaScript runtime that also bundles a package manager, bundler and test runner, built to work as a replacement for Node.js.

butteraugli.label: Butteraugli
butteraugli.plain: Google's perceptual metric that estimates how visible the differences between two images are to a human eye. Lower is better.

bytecode.label: bytecode
bytecode.plain: Compact low-level instructions run by a virtual machine. Compilers turn source code into it.

canvas-api.label: Canvas
canvas-api.plain: The browser's drawing surface for scripts. Its drawImage call can copy an image onto it at a new size.

cdn.label: CDN
cdn.plain: A content delivery network: servers spread around the world that keep copies of a site's files close to visitors so pages load faster.

cdp.label: Chrome DevTools Protocol
cdp.plain: The message protocol Chrome's developer tools use to inspect and control the browser. Automation libraries like Puppeteer use it too.

certificate-authority.label: certificate authority
certificate-authority.plain: An organization browsers trust to issue certificates that vouch a public key belongs to a given website.

character-encoding.label: character encoding
character-encoding.plain: A rule for turning text characters into numbers, and those numbers into bytes, so computers can store and send text.

chi-squared-test.label: chi-squared test
chi-squared-test.plain: A statistic that measures how far a set of observed counts sits from the counts you'd expect; smaller values mean a closer match.

chirality.label: handedness
chirality.plain: The property of a shape that can't be turned to match its own mirror image, like a left hand and a right hand.

chroma-subsampling.label: Chroma subsampling
chroma-subsampling.plain: Storing colour at lower resolution than brightness, since eyes notice brightness detail more. 4:4:4 keeps full colour and 4:2:0 keeps a quarter.

chromium.label: Chromium
chromium.plain: The open-source browser project that Chrome, Edge, Brave and Opera are built on.

ciphertext.label: ciphertext
ciphertext.plain: The scrambled output of encryption, unreadable without the key.

cjk-characters.label: CJK
cjk-characters.plain: Chinese, Japanese and Korean, grouped in computing because their writing systems share a large set of Chinese-derived characters.

ckks.label: CKKS
ckks.plain: A homomorphic encryption scheme by Cheon, Kim, Kim and Song that computes on encrypted real numbers approximately, treating its noise as rounding error.

cloudflare-pages.label: Cloudflare Pages
cloudflare-pages.plain: Cloudflare's hosting service for static websites and front-end apps, deployed straight from a Git repository.

cloudflare-queues.label: Queues
cloudflare-queues.plain: Cloudflare's message queue: one Worker drops tasks in, and another works through them later, in batches and with retries.

cloudflare-workers.label: Cloudflare Workers
cloudflare-workers.plain: Code that runs on Cloudflare's servers around the world and answers each request directly, with no server of the site's own.

cloudflare-workflows.label: Workflows
cloudflare-workflows.plain: A Cloudflare Workers feature for multi-step jobs that saves progress after each step and retries the ones that fail.

cls.label: Cumulative Layout Shift
cls.plain: A score for how much visible content jumps around while a page loads; lower is better, and 0 means nothing moved.

collatz-conjecture.label: Collatz conjecture
collatz-conjecture.plain: An unproven claim that repeatedly halving even numbers and turning odd n into 3n + 1 always reaches 1, from any positive starting number.

colo.label: colo
colo.plain: Short for colocation center, a shared data center. At Cloudflare it means one of the data centers that answers visitors nearby.

compcert.label: CompCert
compcert.plain: A C compiler with a machine-checked proof that the code it produces behaves the way the source program says.

compression-dictionaries.label: Shared dictionary compression
compression-dictionaries.plain: A scheme where the browser keeps an earlier copy of a file and the server sends only a compressed difference against it.

congestion-window.label: Congestion window
congestion-window.plain: How much data a TCP sender may have in flight before it hears back. Connections usually start at 10 packets and grow as replies arrive.

content-addressing.label: Content addressing
content-addressing.plain: Naming each piece of data by a hash of its bytes, so the same content always gets the same name and any change gets a new one.

content-defined-chunking.label: Content-defined chunking
content-defined-chunking.plain: Splitting a file wherever its own bytes match a pattern, so an insertion only moves the boundaries near it and the other chunks stay identical.

content-negotiation.label: content negotiation
content-negotiation.plain: The HTTP mechanism where one URL can answer in different formats, such as HTML or Markdown, depending on what the client says it accepts.

context-window.label: Context window
context-window.plain: The amount of text, counted in tokens, that a language model can take in at once, including its own reply.

control-character.label: control code
control-character.plain: A character code that tells a device to do something instead of printing a symbol, such as a newline, a tab or a backspace.

cookie-store-api.label: Cookie Store API
cookie-store-api.plain: A promise-based browser API for reading and writing cookies, usable from service workers as well as pages.

cpu-cache.label: CPU cache
cpu-cache.plain: A small, fast memory on the processor that keeps copies of recently used data so the chip doesn't have to wait on main memory.

cron-triggers.label: Cron Triggers
cron-triggers.plain: Cloudflare's way to run a Worker on a schedule, like every hour, written in cron syntax.

cryptanalysis.label: cryptanalysis
cryptanalysis.plain: The study and practice of breaking ciphers and recovering secrets without being given the key.

cryptographic-hash-function.label: Hash
cryptographic-hash-function.plain: A short fingerprint computed from data. The same data always gives the same hash, and any change, even one byte, gives a different one.

cryptographic-key.label: cryptographic key
cryptographic-key.plain: A secret value, usually a long random number, that an encryption or signature algorithm uses to lock, unlock or sign data.

cryptographic-primitive.label: cryptographic primitive
cryptographic-primitive.plain: A basic, well-studied building block of cryptography, such as a hash function or a cipher, that larger protocols are built from.

csp.label: Content Security Policy
csp.plain: A header that tells the browser which sources a page may load scripts, styles and other resources from, to block injected code.

css-custom-properties.label: CSS custom properties
css-custom-properties.plain: Variables written in CSS, named with two leading dashes, that other style rules can read and JavaScript can change.

customizable-select.label: customizable select
customizable-select.plain: The CSS value appearance: base-select, which lets a page fully style a native select dropdown, including its open list of options.

d1.label: D1
d1.plain: Cloudflare's SQL database for Workers, built on SQLite.

dac.label: DAC
dac.plain: Digital-to-analog converter: a circuit that turns a stream of numbers into a changing voltage, such as the audio signal that drives headphones.

data-deduplication.label: Deduplication
data-deduplication.plain: Storing identical pieces of data once and pointing to that one copy wherever else they appear.

dct.label: DCT
dct.plain: Discrete cosine transform: math that rewrites a block of pixels as a sum of smooth wave patterns. JPEG stores those wave strengths instead of pixels.

delta-encoding.label: Delta
delta-encoding.plain: Storing or sending only the differences between two versions of data, instead of the whole new version.

denylist.label: denylist
denylist.plain: A list of things to block, where anything not on the list is allowed through by default.

dependency-array.label: dependency array
dependency-array.plain: The list of values a React hook watches; the hook runs again only when one of them changes.

diaphragm.label: diaphragm
diaphragm.plain: The thin membrane in a speaker or headphone that moves back and forth to push air and make sound.

digital-signature.label: digital signature
digital-signature.plain: A value made from a message and a private key that anyone with the matching public key can check, proving who signed it and that it is unchanged.

display-p3.label: Display P3
display-p3.plain: Apple's wide-gamut colour space, which holds more saturated colours than sRGB. iPhones and Macs capture and display in it.

dither.label: dither
dither.plain: Low-level random noise added before rounding a signal, which turns the rounding's patterned distortion into a steady, gentler hiss.

dry-run.label: dry run
dry-run.plain: Running a command so it reports what it would do without actually doing it.

durable-object.label: Durable Object
durable-object.plain: A Cloudflare Workers object with its own built-in storage, where each named instance lives in one place so every request to it is coordinated.

ecdsa.label: ECDSA
ecdsa.plain: A widely used digital signature scheme built on elliptic curves. P-256 is a standard curve commonly paired with it.

ed25519.label: Ed25519
ed25519.plain: A widely used digital signature scheme built on an elliptic curve, with 32-byte public keys and 64-byte signatures that are fast to make and check.

edge.label: the edge
edge.plain: A network of servers spread around the world close to users, so each request is answered from somewhere nearby.

entropy.label: entropy
entropy.plain: A measure of how unpredictable data is. The less predictable the bytes, the less a compressor can shrink them.

es-module.label: ES module
es-module.plain: JavaScript's built-in module format, where files share code through import and export statements.

etag.label: ETag
etag.plain: An HTTP response header that names one exact version of a file, so a cache can ask whether its copy is still current.

eventual-consistency.label: eventual consistency
eventual-consistency.plain: A guarantee that every copy of some data will match in time, while a read right after a write may still return the old value.

evm.label: EVM
evm.plain: The Ethereum Virtual Machine: the computer every Ethereum node simulates to run smart contract bytecode, charging gas for each step.

exif.label: EXIF
exif.plain: Metadata a camera writes into a photo: exposure settings, date, lens, and an Orientation tag saying which way up to show it.

exit-code.label: exit code
exit-code.plain: The number a program reports when it finishes; 0 means success and anything else signals an error.

exploit.label: exploit
exploit.plain: Code or a technique that uses a bug to make a system do something its makers never intended, like leak data or run an attacker's code.

fastcdc.label: FastCDC
fastcdc.plain: A fast content-defined chunking algorithm from a 2016 USENIX paper. It uses a cheap gear hash and tuned masks to pick cut points.

fetch-api.label: fetch
fetch-api.plain: The browser's JavaScript function for requesting a URL from a script and reading the reply.

firmware.label: firmware
firmware.plain: Low-level software stored on a device's chips that starts and controls the hardware, beneath the operating system.

first-paint.label: first paint
first-paint.plain: The moment the browser first draws anything on screen after it starts loading a page.

formal-verification.label: formal verification
formal-verification.plain: Using a computer-checked mathematical proof to show a program or system meets a precise specification for every possible input.

frequency-analysis.label: frequency analysis
frequency-analysis.plain: Breaking a cipher by counting how often each letter appears and matching those counts to a language's known letter frequencies.

fri.label: FRI
fri.plain: Fast Reed-Solomon Interactive Oracle Proof of Proximity: a protocol that lets a verifier check, with few queries, that committed data is close to a low-degree polynomial.

fuzzing.label: fuzzing
fuzzing.plain: Testing a program by feeding it huge numbers of random or mutated inputs and watching for crashes or broken rules.

gamma-correction.label: Gamma
gamma-correction.plain: The curve that maps stored pixel values to light. Files use it to spend more of their levels on dark tones, where eyes are most sensitive.

gear-hash.label: Gear hash
gear-hash.plain: A rolling hash that updates with one shift and one table lookup per byte, cheap enough to run over every byte of a file.

gecko.label: Gecko
gecko.plain: The browser engine inside Firefox that turns HTML, CSS and JavaScript into the page you see.

generics.label: generics
generics.plain: Code written in terms of a type parameter, so one definition, such as a list, works with many specific types.

glyph.label: glyph
glyph.plain: The visual shape drawn for a character in a particular font.

gradual-deployments.label: gradual deployment
gradual-deployments.plain: Moving live traffic to a new version of a Worker a percentage at a time, so the old and new versions serve side by side.

granny-knot.label: granny knot
granny-knot.plain: A knot made of two identical half-knots in a row. It looks like a reef knot but slips or jams under load.

grapheme-cluster.label: grapheme
grapheme-cluster.plain: What a reader sees as one character, even when it is stored as several code points, such as an accented letter or an emoji with a skin tone.

grovers-algorithm.label: Grover's algorithm
grovers-algorithm.plain: A quantum search method that speeds up guessing a secret key, roughly halving its strength: a 256-bit key gives about 128 bits of security.

gsw.label: GSW scheme
gsw.plain: A 2013 fully homomorphic encryption scheme by Gentry, Sahai and Waters, built on learning with errors, whose ciphertexts are matrices.

gzip.label: gzip
gzip.plain: The oldest compression format every browser accepts for web pages. It's fast and universal, and its files come out larger than brotli's or zstd's.

harvest-now-decrypt-later.label: harvest now, decrypt later
harvest-now-decrypt-later.plain: An attack where encrypted traffic is recorded today and stored until a future quantum computer can decrypt it.

headless-browser.label: headless browser
headless-browser.plain: A web browser that runs with no window on screen, driven by code, so a program can load pages, run their scripts and capture the result.

heif.label: HEIF
heif.plain: An image container format, used by iPhones and by Fujifilm's HIF files, that usually holds HEVC-compressed pictures plus their metadata.

high-pass-filter.label: high-pass filter
high-pass-filter.plain: A filter that lets frequencies above a cutoff through and weakens those below it.

hill-climbing.label: hill climbing
hill-climbing.plain: A search that starts from a guess and keeps any small change that improves a score, stopping when no change helps.

hmac.label: HMAC
hmac.plain: A way to tag a message using a shared secret key and a hash function, so anyone holding the key can check the message wasn't changed.

hole-punching.label: hole punching
hole-punching.plain: A trick that lets two devices behind home routers or firewalls connect directly, by having both send packets toward each other at the same time.

htmlrewriter.label: HTMLRewriter
htmlrewriter.plain: A Cloudflare Workers API that edits HTML while it streams through, changing elements on the fly without holding the whole page in memory.

http-304.label: 304 Not Modified
http-304.plain: The HTTP status code saying the browser's cached copy is still current, so the server sends no body.

http-402.label: 402 Payment Required
http-402.plain: An HTTP status code set aside for payments and long left undefined. Some sites now send it to crawlers they want to charge.

http-403.label: 403 Forbidden
http-403.plain: The HTTP status code meaning the server understood the request and refuses to serve it.

http-cache.label: HTTP cache
http-cache.plain: The browser's store of earlier responses, which it reuses instead of downloading again for as long as the server's cache headers allow.

http-message-signatures.label: HTTP Message Signatures
http-message-signatures.plain: A standard way to sign parts of an HTTP request, so the receiver can check who sent it and that nobody altered it on the way.

huffman-coding.label: Huffman coding
huffman-coding.plain: A lossless coding method that gives short bit codes to common symbols and longer ones to rare symbols, shrinking the total.

hydration.label: hydration
hydration.plain: Making server-rendered HTML interactive by running a framework's JavaScript over it in the browser to attach state and event handlers.

hypermedia.label: hypermedia
hypermedia.plain: Hypertext extended with images, sound and video; on the web, pages whose links and forms tell the reader what they can do next.

icc-profile.label: ICC profile
icc-profile.plain: A block of data in an image file that describes its colour space, so software knows how to turn the stored numbers into real colours.

image-histogram.label: histogram
image-histogram.plain: A graph of how many pixels in an image fall at each brightness level, from shadows on the left to highlights on the right.

image-scaling.label: Resampling
image-scaling.plain: Computing a new grid of pixels for an image at a different size, estimating each new pixel from the old ones around it.

immutable.label: immutable
immutable.plain: A Cache-Control setting that tells the browser a file will never change, so it can skip checking for a newer copy.

imperative-programming.label: imperative programming
imperative-programming.plain: Writing code as step-by-step commands that change state directly, such as create this element, then move it.

intel-sgx.label: Intel SGX
intel-sgx.plain: Software Guard Extensions: Intel processor instructions that let a program create an enclave, a region of memory the rest of the system can't read.

jailbreak.label: jailbreaking
jailbreak.plain: Removing the software limits Apple puts on its devices, usually through a security flaw, so the owner can run code Apple hasn't approved.

jpeg.label: JPEG
jpeg.plain: The standard photo format since 1992. It shrinks images by discarding fine detail the eye is unlikely to miss.

jpeg-xl.label: JPEG XL
jpeg-xl.plain: A newer image format from the JPEG committee. It compresses well, decodes in parallel, and can repack an existing JPEG losslessly into a smaller file.

jpegli.label: jpegli
jpegli.plain: Google's JPEG library, a drop-in libjpeg replacement that writes ordinary JPEG files smaller than older encoders at the same visual quality.

jspi.label: JSPI
jspi.plain: JavaScript Promise Integration: a WebAssembly feature that lets synchronous Wasm code pause while it waits on a JavaScript promise, then resume.

jwks.label: JWKS
jwks.plain: JSON Web Key Set: a standard JSON document that publishes one or more public keys so others can verify signatures.

kasiski-examination.label: Kasiski examination
kasiski-examination.plain: A way to find a repeating key's length by measuring the gaps between repeated chunks of ciphertext; the key length usually divides those gaps.

key-agreement.label: key agreement
key-agreement.plain: The step where two parties who share no secret yet create one together over an open network, then use it to encrypt what follows.

keyframes.label: keyframes
keyframes.plain: The CSS rule that lists an animation's waypoints, such as 0% and 100%, and the styles the browser animates between them.

kryptos.label: Kryptos
kryptos.plain: A sculpture at CIA headquarters, made by Jim Sanborn in 1990, that carries four encrypted passages.

lambda-calculus.label: lambda term
lambda-calculus.plain: A tiny formal language where every computation is built by defining functions and applying them to arguments.

lanczos-resampling.label: Lanczos resampling
lanczos-resampling.plain: A resizing filter that weights nearby pixels with a windowed sinc curve. Lanczos3 reaches three pixels out on each side and keeps images sharp.

lattice.label: lattice
lattice.plain: A regular grid of points in many dimensions. Some problems on lattices, like finding the nearest grid point, are hard enough to build encryption on.

lattice-cryptography.label: lattice-based cryptography
lattice-cryptography.plain: Cryptography built on hard problems about points in a grid with hundreds of dimensions, believed hard even for quantum computers. ML-KEM and ML-DSA use it.

lcp.label: Largest Contentful Paint
lcp.plain: How long after a page starts loading its biggest image or block of text appears on screen.

leading.label: leading
leading.plain: The extra space between lines of text. CSS splits it into two halves, one above the letters and one below, called half-leading.

libavif.label: libavif
libavif.plain: The reference library for reading and writing AVIF files. Its avifenc and avifdec tools wrap whichever AV1 or AV2 codec it was built with.

linear-light.label: Linear light
linear-light.plain: Pixel values proportional to the actual amount of light. Ordinary image files store gamma-encoded values, so averaging those directly gets brightness wrong.

log-profile.label: Log profile
log-profile.plain: A camera recording curve that stores light on a logarithmic scale to keep shadow and highlight detail. Footage looks flat until it is graded.

low-pass-filter.label: Low-pass filter
low-pass-filter.plain: A filter that keeps broad, slow changes and removes fine, rapid ones. Downscaling needs one so detail too small for the new size doesn't become artifacts.

luna.label: Luna
luna.plain: The default visual style of Windows XP, with blue title bars, a green Start button and rounded, glossy controls.

main-thread.label: main thread
main-thread.plain: The single thread where a browser runs a page's JavaScript, handles input and lays out the page, so long work there freezes everything.

masonry.label: Masonry layout
masonry.plain: A layout that stacks items in columns at their natural heights, each filling the gap under the one above, like bricks in a wall.

mathematical-induction.label: induction
mathematical-induction.plain: Proving a statement for every natural number by proving it for 0, then proving that whenever it holds for n it holds for n + 1.

mcp.label: MCP
mcp.plain: Model Context Protocol: an open standard for offering tools and data to AI models through one common interface.

media-queries.label: Media queries
media-queries.plain: CSS rules that apply only when the screen matches a condition, such as a width range, so a page can rearrange itself.

merkle-tree.label: Merkle tree
merkle-tree.plain: A tree of hashes where each parent hashes its children, so one root hash vouches for every piece below it.

minification.label: minification
minification.plain: Stripping spaces, comments and long names out of code so it downloads smaller and still runs the same.

ml-dsa.label: ML-DSA
ml-dsa.plain: A post-quantum digital signature standard from NIST (FIPS 204), built on lattice math. Its keys and signatures are far larger than classical ones.

ml-kem.label: ML-KEM
ml-kem.plain: A post-quantum standard from NIST (FIPS 203) for two parties to set up a shared secret key, built on lattice math.

mozjpeg.label: mozjpeg
mozjpeg.plain: Mozilla's JPEG encoder, which makes smaller standard JPEG files than the reference libjpeg at the same quality.

mpc.label: MPC
mpc.plain: Secure multi-party computation: several parties jointly compute a result from their private inputs without any of them revealing its input to the others.

n-gram.label: n-gram
n-gram.plain: A run of n letters in a row; a quadgram is four. Scoring text by how common its quadgrams are in English measures how language-like it reads.

nextjs.label: Next.js
nextjs.plain: A web framework built on React, with server rendering and routing built in.

nodejs.label: Node.js
nodejs.plain: A program that runs JavaScript outside the browser, widely used for servers and build tools.

normal-mode.label: vibration mode
normal-mode.plain: A pattern in which an object vibrates at one frequency, with some regions moving and others standing still.

nyquist-frequency.label: Nyquist frequency
nyquist-frequency.plain: The finest detail a sampling grid can record: half its sampling rate. In an image, a pattern that alternates every pixel.

oauth.label: OAuth
oauth.plain: A standard that lets you grant an app limited access to your account on another service without giving it your password.

oblivious-transfer.label: oblivious transfer
oblivious-transfer.plain: A protocol where a sender offers several messages and the receiver gets exactly one, without the sender learning which one was taken.

oem.label: OEM
oem.plain: Original equipment manufacturer: here, the company that builds and sells the phone, such as OnePlus or Samsung.

oklch.label: OKLCH
oklch.plain: A CSS color notation built from lightness, chroma and hue, arranged so equal steps in the numbers look like equal steps to the eye.

open-graph.label: Open Graph
open-graph.plain: Meta tags a page uses to name the title, description and preview image that apps show when someone shares its link.

oversampling.label: oversampling
oversampling.plain: Running a converter at many times the needed sample rate, so filtering and noise can move to frequencies far above hearing.

parallax-scrolling.label: parallax scrolling
parallax-scrolling.plain: A scrolling effect where background layers move slower than foreground ones, creating a sense of depth.

pay-per-crawl.label: pay per crawl
pay-per-crawl.plain: A Cloudflare feature that lets a site charge AI crawlers for each page they fetch, answering crawlers that haven't paid with HTTP 402.

peer-to-peer.label: peer-to-peer
peer-to-peer.plain: A network where devices talk directly to each other as equals, instead of each one going through a central server.

percentile.label: percentile
percentile.plain: The value a given share of measurements fall at or under; p75 is the value 75 out of every 100 visits meet or beat.

plaintext.label: plaintext
plaintext.plain: The readable message before it is encrypted, or after it is decrypted.

plonk.label: PLONK
plonk.plain: A general-purpose SNARK from 2019 that proves a computation was done correctly, with one setup reusable for any circuit up to a size limit.

popover-api.label: Popover API
popover-api.plain: A browser API for showing content above the rest of the page, such as menus and tooltips, with built-in show, hide and dismiss behavior.

post-quantum-cryptography.label: post-quantum cryptography
post-quantum-cryptography.plain: Cryptography designed to stay secure against large quantum computers, which could break the public-key schemes in common use today.

postcard.label: postcard
postcard.plain: A compact binary format for Rust that turns data structures into short byte strings and back.

prefers-reduced-motion.label: prefers-reduced-motion
prefers-reduced-motion.plain: A CSS media feature that tells a page the user has asked their system to minimize animation.

preload.label: preload
preload.plain: A link hint that tells the browser to start downloading a file it will need soon, before it would otherwise discover it.

private-key.label: private key
private-key.plain: The secret half of a key pair in public-key cryptography, used to sign or decrypt; its public partner can be shared freely.

progressive-enhancement.label: progressive enhancement
progressive-enhancement.plain: Building a page so its core content works in any browser, then layering extra features on top for browsers that support them.

progressive-jpeg.label: Progressive JPEG
progressive-jpeg.plain: A JPEG saved as several passes over the whole image, coarse first, so a browser can show a rough picture before the download finishes.

pseudo-class.label: pseudo-class
pseudo-class.plain: A CSS selector keyword starting with a colon that matches elements in a certain state, like :hover or :popover-open.

pseudo-element.label: pseudo-element
pseudo-element.plain: A CSS selector for a part of an element that has no tag of its own, such as ::before or a dropdown's picker icon, so it can be styled.

psnr.label: PSNR
psnr.plain: Peak signal-to-noise ratio: a simple score, in decibels, of how far a compressed image's pixels drift from the original. Higher means closer.

public-key-cryptography.label: public-key cryptography
public-key-cryptography.plain: Cryptography with a key pair: a public key anyone can see and a private key kept secret. What one key signs or locks, the other checks or opens.

puppeteer.label: Puppeteer
puppeteer.plain: A JavaScript library for controlling Chrome or Firefox from code: opening pages, clicking, filling forms and taking screenshots.

pwa.label: PWA
pwa.plain: Progressive web app: a website built to install and behave like an app, with offline support, a home-screen icon and its own window.

quantization.label: Quantization
quantization.plain: The lossy step in compression: rounding values to a coarser set of levels. The quantizer setting decides how coarse, trading file size against detail.

quic.label: QUIC
quic.plain: A transport protocol that runs fast, encrypted connections over UDP, with many streams sharing one connection. HTTP/3 is built on it.

r2.label: R2
r2.plain: Cloudflare's object storage for files. It speaks Amazon S3's API and charges nothing for downloading data back out.

raf.label: requestAnimationFrame
raf.plain: A browser API that runs a callback just before the next screen repaint, the usual way to sync JavaScript animation with the display.

react.label: React
react.plain: A JavaScript library from Meta for building user interfaces out of reusable components.

react-suspense.label: Suspense
react-suspense.plain: A React feature that shows a fallback, such as a spinner, while part of the page waits for code or data to load.

reactive-programming.label: reactivity
reactive-programming.plain: A programming style where values that depend on other values update automatically whenever those change.

reconstruction-filter.label: reconstruction filter
reconstruction-filter.plain: The low-pass filter after a DAC that smooths its stepped output into a continuous wave and removes copies of the signal above the audio band.

reef-knot.label: reef knot
reef-knot.plain: A knot made of two opposite half-knots, right over left then left over right, that lies flat and holds. Also called a square knot.

reflow.label: Reflow
reflow.plain: The browser recomputing the size and position of elements on a page, which makes content jump when something like an image finishes loading.

render-blocking.label: render-blocking
render-blocking.plain: A file, usually CSS or JavaScript, that the browser must download and process before it can show the page.

request-destination.label: Request destination
request-destination.plain: A label the browser attaches to each request saying what it's for, such as document, image or script. Requests made with fetch() leave it empty.

resonance.label: resonance
resonance.plain: The tendency of an object to vibrate much more strongly at certain frequencies; in a speaker it shows up as peaks at those pitches.

response.label: Response
response.plain: The JavaScript object a web server or Worker builds to describe its reply: status code, headers and body.

rest-api.label: REST
rest-api.plain: A common style of web API where each URL names a resource and standard HTTP methods such as GET and POST act on it.

reverse-dns.label: reverse DNS
reverse-dns.plain: Looking up the hostname that belongs to an IP address, the opposite of a normal DNS lookup. Big crawlers use it to prove where a request came from.

reverse-proxy.label: reverse proxy
reverse-proxy.plain: A server that sits in front of websites and receives their incoming requests, often adding caching and security on the way.

rom.label: ROM
rom.plain: Read-only memory: storage whose contents are set when the chip is made and can't be rewritten by software.

root-of-trust.label: root of trust
root-of-trust.plain: The small piece of hardware or firmware, often holding a built-in secret key, that every other security check on a device ultimately relies on.

round-trip-time.label: round trip
round-trip-time.plain: One request travelling to a server plus its reply coming back; the time this takes is the round-trip time.

rsa.label: RSA
rsa.plain: A public-key system from 1977 for encryption and signatures, secure because factoring the product of two large primes is hard.

rust-crate.label: crate
rust-crate.plain: Rust's name for a package: a unit of code that compiles together and can be published for other programs to use.

safari-technology-preview.label: Safari Technology Preview
safari-technology-preview.plain: Apple's early-release Safari for developers, updated every few weeks with web features that haven't reached regular Safari yet.

same-origin.label: same-origin policy
same-origin.plain: The browser rule that treats a page's own scheme, host and port as one site, and limits what pages from other origins can read.

sample.label: sample
sample.plain: One measurement of a signal's level at an instant. Digital audio stores sound as tens of thousands of these per second.

samsung-knox.label: Samsung Knox
samsung-knox.plain: Samsung's security platform for its phones and tablets, covering secure boot, encrypted storage and a separate secure folder.

scroll-anchoring.label: scroll anchoring
scroll-anchoring.plain: A browser behavior that keeps what you are reading in place when content loads or grows above it, so the page doesn't jump.

service-bindings.label: Service bindings
service-bindings.plain: A Cloudflare link that lets one Worker call another directly, without a trip over the public internet.

service-worker.label: Service worker
service-worker.plain: A script a site installs in the browser that sits between its pages and the network and can answer requests from a local cache.

sha-256.label: SHA-256
sha-256.plain: A hash function that turns any input into a 256-bit fingerprint. Change one byte of the input and the fingerprint changes completely.

shamir-secret-sharing.label: Shamir's secret sharing
shamir-secret-sharing.plain: A way to split a secret into n shares so that any k of them rebuild it, while fewer than k reveal nothing about it.

shebang.label: shebang
shebang.plain: The #! line at the top of a script that tells the operating system which program should run it.

shim.label: shim
shim.plain: A small layer of code that makes one interface behave like another, so code written for the old one keeps working.

shoelace-knot.label: shoelace knot
shoelace-knot.plain: The bow used to tie shoes: a reef knot tied with two loops, so pulling a free end undoes it.

side-channel-attack.label: side-channel attack
side-channel-attack.plain: An attack that learns secrets by measuring a system's physical side effects while it runs, such as timing, power draw, heat or sound.

signal-quantization.label: quantization
signal-quantization.plain: Rounding a signal's values to a fixed set of levels. The gap between the true value and the rounded one is the quantization error.

simd.label: SIMD
simd.plain: Single instruction, multiple data: CPU instructions that do the same operation on several values at once, packed side by side in one wide register.

sinc-filter.label: sinc filter
sinc-filter.plain: The ideal low-pass filter: it passes everything below a cutoff and nothing above, but its response ripples on forever in time.

single-page-application.label: SPA
single-page-application.plain: A web app that loads one page and then rewrites it with JavaScript as you move around, instead of fetching new pages.

single-precision.label: f32
single-precision.plain: A 32-bit floating-point number, which keeps about seven significant decimal digits.

skippable-frame.label: Skippable frame
skippable-frame.plain: A block inside a zstd stream that carries extra data and is marked so every decoder steps over it without reading it.

slh-dsa.label: SLH-DSA
slh-dsa.plain: A post-quantum digital signature standard from NIST (FIPS 205) that relies only on hash functions. Its public keys are tiny; its signatures are large and slow to make.

smart-contract.label: smart contract
smart-contract.plain: A program stored on a blockchain that runs automatically when called, moving funds or data by its own rules.

smt-solver.label: SMT solver
smt-solver.plain: A program that checks whether a set of logical constraints over numbers and data can all hold at once, and if so finds values that satisfy them.

snr.label: SNR
snr.plain: Signal-to-noise ratio: how much stronger the wanted signal is than the background noise, usually given in decibels.

soc.label: SoC
soc.plain: System on a chip: one chip holding a device's processor, graphics, memory controller and other parts that once sat on separate chips.

software-alpha.label: alpha
software-alpha.plain: An early stage of software, before beta, when features are still incomplete and bugs and breaking changes are expected.

solidity.label: Solidity
solidity.plain: The main programming language for writing smart contracts on Ethereum.

speculation-rules.label: Speculation Rules API
speculation-rules.plain: A browser API where a page lists links the browser may fetch or fully render ahead of time, so the next page appears instantly on click.

square-wave.label: square wave
square-wave.plain: A waveform that jumps between two fixed levels. Mathematically it is a tone plus only its odd harmonics.

srgb.label: sRGB
srgb.plain: The standard colour space for screens and the web. Its values are gamma-encoded, so code 128 holds about a fifth of the light of 255.

ssim.label: SSIM
ssim.plain: Structural similarity: a score up to 1 that compares local brightness, contrast and structure between two images. Closer to 1 means more alike.

ssimulacra2.label: SSIMULACRA2
ssimulacra2.plain: A perceptual image quality score from Cloudinary, built to match how people judge compressed photos. Higher is better, and about 90 is hard to tell from the original.

ssr.label: server-side rendering
ssr.plain: Building a page's HTML on the server for each request, so the browser receives finished markup ready to display.

stale-while-revalidate.label: stale-while-revalidate
stale-while-revalidate.plain: A caching rule: hand out the saved copy right away even after it expires, then fetch a fresh one in the background for next time.

standard-streams.label: stdin
standard-streams.plain: A program's standard input, the stream it reads from by default. A tool that talks over stdin and stdout can be driven by another program.

symbolic-link.label: Symlink
symbolic-link.plain: A file that points to another file or folder by path, so opening it opens the target.

tabula-recta.label: tabula recta
tabula-recta.plain: A 26 by 26 table of alphabets, each row shifted one letter from the last, used to encrypt and decrypt Vigenère-style ciphers by lookup.

tc39.label: TC39
tc39.plain: The committee that designs JavaScript. Proposals advance through numbered stages, and stage 4 means finished and added to the language.

tee.label: TEE
tee.plain: Trusted execution environment: a walled-off area of a processor where code and data stay hidden from the rest of the machine, including the operating system.

temporal.label: Temporal
temporal.plain: A new built-in JavaScript API for dates and times, with proper time zones and calendars, meant to replace the error-prone Date object.

thd.label: THD
thd.plain: Total harmonic distortion: how much of a device's output is harmonics it added to the original tone, as a share of that tone.

tls-handshake.label: TLS handshake
tls-handshake.plain: The opening exchange of a secure web connection, where browser and server agree on encryption keys and the server proves its identity.

trace-span.label: trace span
trace-span.plain: One timed step inside a traced request, with a name, a start time, a duration and attributes. Nested spans show where the time went.

transferable-streams.label: transferable streams
transferable-streams.plain: Streams that can be handed from one thread to another, such as to a worker, so the data moves without being copied.

tree-shaking.label: tree shaking
tree-shaking.plain: A build step that drops code a program never uses, so the shipped bundle contains only what runs.

trellis-quantization.label: Trellis quantization
trellis-quantization.plain: An encoder search that tries alternative rounding choices for each block and keeps whichever gives the best trade of file size against error.

trustzone.label: TrustZone
trustzone.plain: An Arm processor feature that splits the chip into a normal world and a secure world, so sensitive code runs isolated from the main operating system.

ttfb.label: TTFB
ttfb.plain: Time to first byte: how long a browser waits after sending a request before the first byte of the response arrives.

ttl.label: TTL
ttl.plain: Time to live: how long a cached or stored copy counts as fresh before it expires and has to be fetched again.

type-inference.label: type inference
type-inference.plain: A compiler working out the types of values from how they are written and used, without the programmer spelling them out.

typescript.label: TypeScript
typescript.plain: JavaScript with type annotations, checked by a compiler that catches mismatched types before the code runs.

undefined-behavior.label: undefined behavior
undefined-behavior.plain: Program operations a language standard gives no meaning to, such as reading past the end of an array, so a compiler may do anything with them.

user-agent.label: User-Agent
user-agent.plain: The request header where a browser or bot names itself on every web request. It is plain text, so any client can claim any name.

vary.label: Vary
vary.plain: A response header telling caches which request headers changed the answer, so they keep a separate copy for each variant.

view-transitions.label: View Transition API
view-transitions.plain: A browser API that animates the change between two views or two pages by snapshotting the old one and morphing into the new.

viewport.label: viewport
viewport.plain: The part of a web page currently visible in the browser window; anything outside it needs scrolling to see.

vinext.label: Vinext
vinext.plain: A Vite plugin from Cloudflare that reimplements the Next.js API, so Next.js apps can build with Vite and deploy to Workers or elsewhere.

virtual-dom.label: virtual DOM
virtual-dom.plain: An in-memory copy of the page's structure that a framework compares against, to work out the smallest set of real changes to make.

vmaf.label: VMAF
vmaf.plain: Netflix's video quality score, which combines several measurements into one 0 to 100 number that predicts how viewers would rate the picture.

voice-coil.label: voice coil
voice-coil.plain: A coil of wire fixed to a speaker cone that moves in a magnet's field when audio current flows through it, driving the cone.

voltage-divider.label: voltage divider
voltage-divider.plain: Resistors in series that output a fixed fraction of the input voltage, set by the ratio of their resistances.

web-bot-auth.label: Web Bot Auth
web-bot-auth.plain: A proposed standard where a bot signs each HTTP request with its private key and publishes the public key, so websites can check which bot sent it.

web-crawler.label: web crawler
web-crawler.plain: A program that fetches web pages automatically, for a search engine, an AI company or an archive.

web-crypto.label: Web Crypto
web-crypto.plain: The browser's built-in cryptography toolkit for scripts, offering hashing, encryption and signatures.

web-font.label: web font
web-font.plain: A font file a site sends along with its pages, so text shows in that typeface even when the reader's device lacks it.

webassembly.label: WebAssembly
webassembly.plain: A compact binary format for code that browsers and other runtimes run at near-native speed, usually compiled from languages like Rust or C++.

webkit.label: WebKit
webkit.plain: The open-source browser engine that powers Safari.

webp.label: WebP
webp.plain: Google's image format for the web. It usually compresses better than JPEG and not as well as AVIF.

worker-isolate.label: isolate
worker-isolate.plain: A lightweight sandbox inside one runtime process where a Cloudflare Worker's code runs, walled off from other code and reused across requests.

workerd.label: workerd
workerd.plain: Cloudflare's open-source runtime that runs Workers code, both in production and on a developer's own machine.

workers-ai.label: Workers AI
workers-ai.plain: Cloudflare's service for running machine-learning models, such as language and vision models, on its own GPUs, called directly from a Worker.

workers-cache-api.label: Workers Cache API
workers-cache-api.plain: The interface a Cloudflare Worker uses to store responses in the local data center's cache and serve them on later requests.

workers-free.label: Workers Free
workers-free.plain: Cloudflare's no-cost Workers plan. It allows 100,000 requests a day and 10 ms of CPU time per request.

workers-kv.label: Workers KV
workers-kv.plain: Cloudflare's key-value store: values saved under names and copied worldwide, so reads are fast everywhere while a new write can take a minute to spread.

workers-logs.label: Workers Logs
workers-logs.plain: Cloudflare's built-in log store for Workers. It collects each request's log lines so you can search and filter them in the dashboard.

wrangler.label: Wrangler
wrangler.plain: Cloudflare's command-line tool for developing, configuring and deploying Workers.

wwdc.label: WWDC
wwdc.plain: Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference, held each June, where it announces new operating systems and developer tools.

xslt.label: XSLT
xslt.plain: A language for transforming XML documents into other formats, such as HTML. Browsers have been able to run it natively for decades.

zenjpeg.label: zenjpeg
zenjpeg.plain: A JPEG encoder and decoder in Rust from Imazen. It began as a port of Google's jpegli and adds perceptual tuning and trellis quantization.

zlib.label: zlib
zlib.plain: A widely used compression library. Node.js names its built-in compression module after it, and that module also covers brotli and zstd.

zstd.label: zstd
zstd.plain: Zstandard, a compression algorithm from Meta built for very fast decompression. Browsers accept it as a way to shrink web pages in transit.

zstd-trained-dictionary.label: Trained dictionary
zstd-trained-dictionary.plain: A zstd dictionary built by zstd --train from sample files. It holds their most common byte patterns and an ID that each compressed frame records.

zwj.label: zero-width joiner
zwj.plain: An invisible Unicode character that joins its neighbors, used to combine several emoji into one, such as a family.
